1.headline: Bahrain Says It Stopped Attacks From Iran
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Why did sirens ring all over Bahrain on Sunday?
Bahrain is a small country in the Gulf. Its army said Iran attacked it from the air. Bahrain stopped the attacks. They did not hit their targets.
Iran told a different story. It said it sent six drones. A drone is a small plane with no pilot. Iran said the drones flew to an American base. But no one said the base was hit.
People heard loud booms. The government told them to stay calm. They went to safe places.
The United States and Israel are at war with Iran. The war started in February. There is no peace deal yet.
Again, Bahrain says it stopped attacks from Iran. This could make the war bigger again.
Thank you for listening.

2.headline: Bahrain Says It Stopped Iranian Drone Attacks
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Early on Sunday, loud sirens and explosions woke people up in Bahrain.

Bahrain is a small island country in the Gulf. According to news reports, its military said Iran attacked it from the air. Bahrain's air defenses stopped the attacks. Air defenses are weapons that shoot down drones and missiles. The military said the attacks did not reach their targets.

Iran told a different story. Its Revolutionary Guard is a powerful military group. It said it sent six drones to an American radar at a helicopter base. A radar finds planes and missiles in the sky. But the United States and Bahrain did not say the radar was hit. There were no quick reports of injuries.
The government asked people to stay calm and go to a safe place.
The United States and Israel have been at war with Iran since February. The fighting is slower now, but peace talks have no deal yet. Bahrain is home to a large base of the United States Navy.
To sum up, Bahrain says it stopped Iranian drone attacks. Iran says it aimed at an American base. This news shows the war could grow again.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: Bahrain Says It Shot Down Iranian Drone Attacks
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Why did sirens sound across the small Gulf country of Bahrain early on Sunday?

According to news reports, Bahrain's military said its air defenses stopped several Iranian attacks from the air. Air defenses are weapons that shoot down missiles and drones. The military said the attacks were destroyed before they reached their targets. It also accused Iran of acting in a hostile, or unfriendly, way toward Bahrain again and again.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard, a powerful military force, told a different story. It said it sent six drones toward an American radar system at a helicopter base in Bahrain. A radar uses radio waves to find planes and missiles. However, neither the United States nor Bahrain confirmed that the radar was hit, and there were no immediate reports of injuries.
During the attacks, people heard explosions, and the government told residents to stay calm and go to a safe place.

Here is some background. Bahrain is home to the headquarters of the United States Navy's Fifth Fleet. The United States and Israel have been at war with Iran since February. The fighting has slowed down in recent weeks, but peace talks have not produced a deal yet. On the same day, Saudi Arabia also said it stopped missiles fired by the Houthis, a group in Yemen that is close to Iran.
Why does this matter? The Gulf region is very important for the world's oil and shipping. New attacks could break the fragile calm and slow down efforts to end the war.
To sum up, Bahrain says it stopped several Iranian drone attacks, while Iran says it targeted an American base. The news shows how easily the conflict could heat up again.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.

보도에 따르면 바레인 군은 자국 방공망이 이란의 공중 공격 여러 건을 막았다고 밝혔습니다. 방공망은 미사일과 드론을 쏘아 떨어뜨리는 무기입니다. 군은 공격이 목표물에 닿기 전에 파괴됐다고 말했습니다. 또 이란이 바레인에 거듭 적대적인, 즉 우호적이지 않은 태도를 보인다고 비난했습니다.
강력한 군사 조직인 이란 혁명수비대의 이야기는 달랐습니다. 혁명수비대는 바레인의 한 헬기 기지에 있는 미국 레이더 시스템을 향해 드론 6대를 보냈다고 말했습니다. 레이더는 전파로 비행기와 미사일을 찾아내는 장치입니다. 하지만 미국도 바레인도 레이더가 맞았다고 확인하지 않았고, 부상자가 있다는 소식도 바로 나오지 않았습니다.
공격이 이어지는 동안 사람들은 폭발음을 들었고, 정부는 주민들에게 침착하게 안전한 곳으로 가라고 했습니다.

이 소식은 왜 중요할까요? 걸프 지역은 세계의 석유와 해상 운송에 매우 중요합니다. 새로운 공격은 아슬아슬한 평온을 깨고 전쟁을 끝내려는 노력을 늦출 수 있습니다.
정리하면, 바레인은 이란의 드론 공격 여러 건을 막았다고 말하고, 이란은 미군 기지를 겨냥했다고 말합니다. 이 소식은 분쟁이 얼마나 쉽게 다시 달아오를 수 있는지 보여 줍니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Bahrain Intercepts Iranian Drones as Tehran Claims Strike on U.S. Base
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Bahrain says it has fought off a fresh wave of Iranian drone attacks, the second scare for the Gulf kingdom in just three days.

According to news reports, Bahrain's military said early on Sunday that its air defenses intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks before they could reach their targets. In a statement, the military accused Tehran of a systematic hostile approach toward the kingdom. Explosions and sirens were reported across the country, and the Interior Ministry urged residents to stay calm and head to the nearest safe location.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard offered a very different account. Iranian state media said the Guard launched six drones at a U.S. air defense radar at the Riffa helicopter base. So far, neither Washington nor Bahraini officials have confirmed that the radar was struck, and there have been no immediate reports of casualties.

The incident follows a similar claim on Friday, when the Revolutionary Guard said it had destroyed an American early-warning radar in Bahrain. U.S. Central Command disputed that claim, saying it had intercepted two Iranian drones and that no one was hurt.

Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, making it a key partner for Washington in the region. The United States and Israel have been at war with Iran since late February. Although fighting has eased in recent weeks, diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough. On the same day, a Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed ballistic missiles fired by Yemen's Houthi rebels toward Riyadh.
The latest attacks matter well beyond the Gulf. The region is vital to global oil supplies and shipping, and any new escalation could threaten the fragile lull and complicate peace talks.
To sum up, Bahrain says it stopped several Iranian drone attacks, while Iran claims it targeted a U.S. radar site. The exchange is a reminder of how quickly the conflict could flare up again.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Bahrain Repels Iranian Drone Barrage as Tehran Claims Hit on U.S. Radar
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
For the second time in three days, air-raid sirens have wailed across Bahrain, as the tiny Gulf kingdom says it repelled a fresh barrage of Iranian drones.

According to news reports, Bahrain's military announced on Sunday that its air defenses had intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks before they could reach their intended targets. In unusually blunt language, it accused Tehran of a systematic hostile approach toward the kingdom. As explosions echoed in the pre-dawn hours, the Interior Ministry urged residents to remain calm, seek out the nearest safe location and rely only on official channels for information.

Tehran, unsurprisingly, told a different story. Iranian state media reported that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps had dispatched six drones against a U.S. air defense radar at the Riffa helicopter base. Neither Washington nor Manama has corroborated the claim that the radar was hit, and there were no immediate reports of casualties.

The episode bears a striking resemblance to Friday's events, when the Guard boasted of destroying an American early-warning radar in Bahrain, only for U.S. Central Command to counter that it had downed two Iranian drones without any injuries or damage.

Bahrain's strategic weight far exceeds its size. It hosts the headquarters of the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet, which makes it an obvious lightning rod in a war that the United States and Israel have waged against Iran since late February. Although the fighting has subsided into a broader lull, diplomatic efforts to bring the conflict to a close have so far failed to yield a breakthrough. Underscoring the regional tension, a Saudi-led coalition said on the same day that it had shot down ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Houthi rebels toward Riyadh.

The stakes extend far beyond the Gulf. The region sits at the heart of global energy markets and shipping lanes, and every fresh flare-up risks unravelling the uneasy calm and muddying negotiations that are already on shaky ground.

To sum up, Bahrain says it thwarted several Iranian drone attacks, while Tehran insists it struck at a U.S. military target. Whatever the truth, the tit-for-tat claims show just how precarious the region's fragile calm remains.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: Giant Arms Catch a Spaceship
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Can a tower catch a spaceship in the air? Yes, it can!
The company SpaceX has a very big rocket. Its name is Starship. Starship went into space on Friday. It flew around the Earth.
On Saturday, the top part came back to Texas. It came down slowly. Then two huge metal arms caught it in the air. People call the arms "chopsticks." This was the first time ever.
The bottom part of the rocket did not come back. It blew up over the sea.
Why is this big news? A rocket you can use again costs less. One day, Starship may take people to the Moon.
Again, giant arms caught Starship in the air. It was a first.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: SpaceX Catches a Returning Starship in Midair for the First Time
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.

4.headline: SpaceX Catches Starship in Midair After Orbital Flight
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
SpaceX has pulled off something no one had done before: catching a giant spaceship in midair as it returned from orbit.

According to news reports, the company's Starship spacecraft flew back to its launch pad at Starbase, Texas, on Saturday, about twenty-two hours after lifting off. As the ship descended with its engines still firing, a pair of enormous mechanical arms on the launch tower, nicknamed the chopsticks, closed around it and held it in place.

It was the first time a Starship had been captured on its return from space. SpaceX has caught the rocket's first-stage booster several times since 2024, but the upper stage had never been caught until now. The flight was not a complete success, however. The booster exploded over the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Friday's liftoff, so SpaceX fell short of the double catch it had hoped for.
Still, the reaction was enthusiastic. SpaceX commentators and crowds watching nearby cheered, and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman described the moment as almost magic.

Starship is the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing taller than most office buildings, and SpaceX's goal is to make it fully reusable, like a commercial airliner. Recovering both stages intact would dramatically cut the cost of each launch and allow rockets to fly far more often.

That matters well beyond SpaceX. NASA is counting on Starship to land astronauts on the Moon later this decade, and company founder Elon Musk has long said he wants the rocket to carry people to Mars.

To sum up, SpaceX used its launch tower's giant arms to catch Starship in midair after an orbital flight, a first in spaceflight history, even though the booster was lost. The milestone brings fully reusable rockets a step closer.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Starship Plucked From the Sky in a Spaceflight First
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

According to news reports, the ship touched back down at Starbase, the company's launch site in south Texas, on Saturday, roughly twenty-two hours after it blasted off. As it descended, engines still blazing, a pair of colossal mechanical arms on the launch tower, affectionately dubbed the chopsticks, swung shut and cradled the vehicle in midair.

The catch marked the first time a Starship had been plucked from the air on its return from space. SpaceX has repeatedly snagged the rocket's first-stage booster since 2024, but the upper stage had never been recovered this way. The mission was not without its setbacks: the booster blew apart over the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Friday's liftoff, denying the company the double catch it had been angling for.

That did little to dampen the mood. Spectators gathered nearby erupted in cheers, and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman hailed the moment as almost magic. SpaceX's own mission commentators were equally jubilant.
Did you know? Starship is the tallest and most powerful rocket ever flown, standing higher than most office towers.

The significance goes well beyond spectacle. Traditionally, rocket stages have been used only once, burning up or plunging into the ocean, which makes every launch eye-wateringly expensive. SpaceX's entire strategy rests on turning rockets into something closer to airliners, refuelled and reflown rather than discarded after a single use. Recovering both stages intact would slash launch costs and make far more frequent flights feasible.
The stakes are high for NASA, too, which is banking on Starship to put astronauts back on the Moon later this decade, while Elon Musk has long envisioned the vehicle ferrying settlers to Mars.

To sum up, SpaceX has caught a returning Starship in midair for the first time, notching a landmark achievement despite losing its booster along the way. The feat moves the dream of fully reusable mega rockets tantalisingly closer to reality.
Thank you for listening.

2.headline: Tax Exam's Top Scorer Admits Cheating With AI
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
How did one man get almost a perfect score on a very hard test?

According to news reports, the top scorer of this year's tax accountant exam in Korea has admitted that he cheated. Tax accountants help people and companies with their taxes. The exam is famous for being very difficult.
On Sunday, the man, who is thirty-four, said sorry in a video. He also gave a written confession to the police. A confession means telling the truth about doing something wrong.

He said he used a tiny camera to take pictures of the questions. The pictures went to an AI tool, and he checked the answers on a smartphone. In the first round, he scored 397.5 out of 400. Before, he said he did not cheat.
The police are now investigating. The agency that runs the exam said sorry for not stopping him.
This news comes just days before the national college entrance exam, called the Suneung, on Thursday. People worry that AI makes cheating easier.
To sum up, the top scorer of a hard national exam says he cheated with AI. Now test rules may become stricter.
Thank you for listening.

일요일, 34세인 이 남성은 영상으로 사과했습니다. 경찰에 자필 자백서도 냈습니다. 자백이란 잘못한 일에 대해 사실을 털어놓는 것입니다.
그는 아주 작은 카메라로 문제를 찍었다고 말했습니다. 사진은 AI 도구로 보내졌고, 그는 스마트폰으로 답을 확인했습니다. 1차 시험에서 그는 400점 만점에 397.5점을 받았습니다. 전에는 부정행위를 하지 않았다고 말했습니다.
경찰은 지금 수사하고 있습니다. 시험을 운영하는 기관은 그를 막지 못한 것을 사과했습니다.
이 소식은 목요일 대학수학능력시험, 즉 수능을 며칠 앞두고 나왔습니다. 사람들은 AI 때문에 부정행위가 쉬워질까 걱정합니다.
정리하면, 어려운 국가 시험의 수석 합격자가 AI로 부정행위를 했다고 말했습니다. 이제 시험 규칙이 더 엄격해질 수 있습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: Top Scorer on Korea's Tax Accountant Exam Admits AI Cheating
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
A near-perfect score on one of Korea's toughest professional exams turned out to be the product of a hidden camera and artificial intelligence.

According to news reports, the top scorer on this year's certified tax accountant exam has admitted to cheating, reversing his earlier denials. The thirty-four-year-old made the confession on Sunday in a video posted on his lawyer's YouTube channel and submitted a written statement to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency.

He said he used a miniature camera to photograph the exam questions, sent the images to an AI tool and then read the answers on a smartphone. He declined to give further details, saying he did not want others to copy the method. He also admitted using the same technique in the first round of the certified public accountant exam in March.

His results had already raised eyebrows. In the first round of the tax exam in April, he scored 397.5 out of 400, answering 159 of 160 multiple-choice questions correctly. Online suspicions had focused on AI smart glasses, but he said that was not how he did it.

Police have launched an investigation, and the exam's administrator, HRD Korea, has apologized for failing to prevent the cheating. News reports say the agency is pursuing a criminal complaint against him.

The timing has heightened public concern. The case comes just days before Thursday's College Scholastic Ability Test, known as the Suneung, which hundreds of thousands of students will sit. Officials are under pressure to show that exam rooms can keep pace with fast-changing technology.
To sum up, the top scorer on Korea's tax accountant exam says he cheated with a hidden camera and AI, and police are investigating. The case is prompting calls for tighter exam security nationwide.
Thank you for listening.
